title_en: Mo Junfei v. Li Kaoxing — divorce dispute
ruling_gist_en: A divorce agreement reached between spouses is a formal contract, meaning that the divorce agreement becomes effective only when both parties reach a consensus on divorce and sign the agreement. The parties' disposition of property is premised on the conclusion of divorce. Although the formalities for the transfer of property rights have been completed, the divorce agreement is not effective because the precondition of divorce is not satisfied, and the property whose rights have been transferred still constitutes community property during the marriage.

full_text_en:
Mo Junfei v. Li Kaoxing — divorce dispute

Ruling Summary

An agreement on divorce reached between the parties to a marriage is a formal agreement, that is, the divorce agreement takes effect only when the parties reach a mutual agreement to divorce and sign the agreement. The parties' handling of property is premised on the achievement of divorce. Even though the procedures for changing the rights to property have been carried out, the property for which the right holder has been changed still constitutes community property during the existence of the marital relationship because the precondition of divorce is not satisfied and the agreement has not taken effect.

Plaintiff: Mo Junfei, female, Han Chinese, 31 years old, residing at Wenlang Residents' Committee, Wenlang Town, Huaiji County, Guangdong Province.

Defendant: Li Kaoxing, male, Han Chinese, 34 years old, residing at Henan Residents' Committee, Chengnan, Huaicheng Town, Huaiji County, Guangdong Province.

The plaintiff, Mo Junfei, filed a lawsuit with the People's Court of Huaiji County, Guangdong Province, due to a divorce dispute with the defendant, Li Kaoxing.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff and the defendant, Li Kaoxing, became acquainted through an introduction in the first half of 2002, registered their marriage in March 2003, and gave birth to a son, Li Xuyu, on October 21 of the same year. Due to a lack of understanding before marriage and a hasty union, their personalities were completely incompatible after marriage. The defendant is selfish and suspicious in character and treats his wife as personal property. As a teacher, the plaintiff inevitably exchanges a few words when meeting classmates, colleagues, or students' parents, but the defendant interferes with and restricts the plaintiff's normal social interactions, speaks harshly to the plaintiff, and even insults the plaintiff's dignity. Usually, there is little heart-to-heart communication between the plaintiff and the defendant. When the plaintiff is ill, the defendant is indifferent. The parties have been completely unable to establish the proper marital affection. During the summer vacation of 2007, the plaintiff proposed to go out to do tutoring to support the family and alleviate marital conflicts, but the defendant objected. The plaintiff's mother even intervened to stop the plaintiff from going out, declaring, "If you want to do tutoring outside, you must first go through divorce procedures," and so on. As the marital affection between the plaintiff and the defendant deteriorated continuously, the parties once agreed to divorce in May 2010, but the negotiation failed on issues such as property division. In July 2010, in order to monopolize the community property upon divorce, the defendant deceived the plaintiff into transferring all the land use rights within the scope of the (2006) No. 0036 Land Use Certificate under the plaintiff's name to the defendant. In early August 2010, the defendant drove the plaintiff out of the home and replaced all the locks. The plaintiff was forced to rent a house outside and live with her son. The marital affection between the plaintiff and the defendant has completely broken down, with no possibility of reconciliation. The plaintiff firmly demands a divorce. The property during the existence of the marital relationship includes a homestead located at Yu Xiu Residents' Committee, Huaicheng Town (land use rights within the scope of the (2006) No. 0036 Land Use Certificate) valued at RMB 150,000, as well as electrical appliances, furniture, etc., which should be divided according to law. Therefore, the plaintiff hereby files a lawsuit with the court, requesting: 1. a judgment granting the divorce between the plaintiff and the defendant; 2. custody of the son Li Xuyu to be awarded to the plaintiff, with child support expenses to be borne jointly by the plaintiff and the defendant; 3. an equal division of the community property (valued at approximately RMB 150,000) according to law; and 4. the court acceptance fee to be borne by the defendant.

Defendant's Defense: The plaintiff, Mo Junfei, and the defendant became acquainted through an introduction and then dated freely for a year, during which both parties fully understood each other's personalities, thus having a solid premarital foundation. After marriage, the parties gave birth to a son, Li Xuyu. The defendant twice used his connections to transfer the plaintiff's job. In December 2009, the plaintiff was hospitalized for 15 days due to illness, and the defendant accompanied her every day until she recovered, demonstrating deep and solid marital affection. There is still a possibility of reconciliation between the plaintiff and the defendant. The defendant firmly opposes the divorce and requests that the judge do more ideological work on the plaintiff to make her abandon the idea of divorce and save the marriage between the plaintiff and the defendant.

Facts Found by the Court from the First Instance of the People's Court of Huaiji County, Guangdong Province:

The plaintiff, Mo Junfei, and the defendant, Li Kaoxing, became acquainted through an introduction in the first half of 2002, registered their marriage in March 2003, and gave birth to a son, Li Xuyu, on October 21 of the same year. After marriage, the marital affection between the plaintiff and the defendant was relatively good. During the summer vacation of 2007, Li Kaoxing prevented Mo Junfei from going out to do tutoring, and a verbal altercation arose between the parties. Thereafter, the marital relationship fluctuated between good and bad. In May 2010, Mo Junfei drafted a divorce agreement and gave it to Li Kaoxing. Li Kaoxing agreed to go through the divorce procedures if the son would be raised by him and the homestead purchased during the existence of the marriage (with the use right registered in the wife's name, valued at RMB 200,000) would belong to the husband. In July of the same year, the parties went to the land administration department and transferred all the land use rights originally registered under Mo Junfei's name within the scope of the (2006) No. 0036 Land Use Certificate to Li Kaoxing's name. However, Li Kaoxing later reneged and refused to divorce. In early August of the same year, Mo Junfei moved out of the home and lived in a rented house, then filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting a judgment granting divorce and a division of community property.

After mediation presided over by the People's Court of Huaiji County, Guangdong Province, since the plaintiff, Mo Junfei, insisted on divorce while the defendant, Li Kaoxing, refused to agree to divorce, mediation was unsuccessful.

The focus of the dispute in this case at first instance was: whether the divorce agreement drafted by the plaintiff, Mo Junfei, and the defendant, Li Kaoxing, was effective, and whether the property after the change of rights still constituted community property.

Opinion of the Court from the First Instance of the People's Court of Huaiji County, Guangdong Province:

The plaintiff, Mo Junfei, and the defendant, Li Kaoxing, became acquainted and fell in love through an introduction. After a period of mutual understanding, they voluntarily registered their marriage, establishing a good emotional foundation. After marriage, the plaintiff and the defendant supported each other in life and work, forming a certain degree of marital affection. The son born to them is still young. From the circumstances reflected in the litigation, the son urgently needs the care of both parents. A divorce between the parties would cause harm to the son. Therefore, the claim for divorce filed by Mo Junfei is not supported.

With regard to the issue of whether the parties reached a divorce agreement. A divorce agreement is an agreement that terminates the personal relationship between husband and wife. This agreement is a formal agreement that must be signed and confirmed by both parties to take effect; that is, the signing and affixing of seals by both parties on the agreement is a prerequisite for its establishment. Otherwise, even if a witness is present to testify that the parties have reached a mutual agreement to divorce, since one party has not signed and confirmed the divorce agreement, the divorce agreement is, in law, not established. The plaintiff, Mo Junfei, drafted a divorce agreement in May 2010 and gave it to the defendant, Li Kaoxing. Although Li Kaoxing verbally agreed to divorce and the parties performed part of the division of community property, it can be determined that the parties reached a mutual agreement on divorce. However, because Li Kaoxing did not sign the agreement, the divorce agreement lacked the essential elements for the formation of a contract. Moreover, Li Kaoxing later reneged and refused to divorce. Therefore, the court cannot grant a divorce based solely on a divorce agreement signed by only one party.

With regard to the issue of the parties' handling of property before divorce. The divorce agreement in this case is a marital divorce agreement. The so-called marital divorce agreement refers to an agreement reached by a man and a woman during the existence of their marital relationship, with the basic purpose of dissolving the marriage, and addressing issues of property division and child custody. A marital divorce agreement is premised on the parties' mutual agreement to divorce. To achieve the goal of divorce, one or both parties may make conditional concessions on issues such as child custody or property division. Where the parties have not registered the divorce with the marriage registration authority, the agreement has not taken effect and has no legally binding force on either party. The terms concerning child custody and property division in the agreement cannot be taken as direct grounds for the people's court to handle divorce cases. The handling of property division by the plaintiff, Mo Junfei, and the defendant, Li Kaoxing, through negotiation during the process of agreeing to divorce was a true expression of their intentions, and the change of registration has already been carried out. However, because Li Kaoxing did not sign the divorce agreement, the essential elements for the formation of the divorce agreement were not met. Therefore, the marital divorce agreement is void, and the performance carried out pursuant to that agreement can also be deemed void. Although the land use rights within the scope of the (2006) No. 0036 Land Use Certificate have been changed to Li Kaoxing's name, those land use rights remain community property during the existence of the marriage between Mo Junfei and Li Kaoxing, and the nature is the same as when they were originally registered under Mo Junfei's name.

In summary, as long as the parties cherish the already established marital affection, treat marriage and family issues with caution, and show mutual respect and care, there is a possibility of reconciliation. Accordingly, the People's Court of Huaiji County, Guangdong Province, in accordance with Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 32, Paragraph 2 of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on December 2, 2010:

The plaintiff Mo Junfei's claim for divorce is dismissed.

The court acceptance fee is RMB 150, to be borne by the plaintiff, Mo Junfei.

After the first-instance judgment, neither the plaintiff, Mo Junfei, nor the defendant, Li Kaoxing, appealed, and the judgment has taken legal effect.
